## v1.166.4

Unofficial custom build based on the exact official [Storj v1.166.4](https://github.com/storj/storj/releases/tag/v1.166.4) source, commit `b2fe6e00c07c42711217c1c60c283d5e000b18ba`. This is not an official Storj Labs release.

The tag and embedded version match the corresponding official Storj version without a custom suffix. This updates the previous custom v1.165.6 build; the repository, Git commit and build attestations distinguish these binaries from official ones.

### Differences from official v1.166.4

- Keep the existing opt-in hashstore compaction salvage implementation instead of layering upstream's new truncated-record handling on top of it. Salvage preserves readable records, discards only records proven unreadable or outside a truncated log, and reports committed losses through amnesty with `READ_FAILURE`. Linux `ENODATA` is confirmed by repeated source reads. Protective limits apply across the complete compaction, and fatal errors still abort the current round.
- Expose compaction progress, rewritten/reclaimed bytes, and salvage counters through `GET /api/sno/compaction`.
- Correct compaction ETA during ordered record rewriting.
- Refresh the satellite trust pool before hashstore recovery and amnesty reporting at startup.
- Add optional target free-space reporting to satellites, with no change to local disk-space calculations.
- Add opt-in manual log compaction. Automatic startup, load-triggered, and periodic maintenance still run in `table-only` mode and apply Bloom filters, expiration, restore, and trash state. Full compaction can be started asynchronously through an authenticated API and processes satellite stores sequentially.
- Normalize satellite storage-usage gaps in Multinode responses using the same normalization as the upstream node dashboard. Dashboard and estimated-payout normalization are already part of official Storj and are not patched again.

### Salvage behavior and compatibility

**Unlike official v1.166.4, this build does not automatically discard truncated records when `hashstore.compaction.salvage` is disabled.** The flag remains disabled by default, matching the previous custom releases. Enabling it activates the existing guarded salvage for both truncation and confirmed source-read failures. No additional unguarded upstream discard path is used.

The salvage algorithm, limits, manual compaction API, and existing configuration retain their previous behavior. The new upstream truncated-record regression test is retained with salvage enabled and checks `READ_FAILURE` reporting for both table backends and ordered/unordered rewriting.

The other upstream v1.166.4 changes are retained, including whole-piece reads for small hashstore pieces, skipping disk reads for canceled downloads, server connection-setup fixes, disabling MPTCP on listeners, and dependency security updates. The custom patches introduce no additional database migration or hashstore format change.

### Docker rollback notice

The [reported unintended downgrades](https://forum.storj.io/t/there-seem-to-be-problems-with-the-update-to-1-166-4/33083/13) concern the official Docker entrypoint's selection of persisted/runtime binaries, not an intentional downgrade by the updater's version comparison. The two-directory implementation dates to [Docker PR #25, merged on October 3, 2024](https://github.com/storj/storagenode-docker/pull/25); related restart/database compatibility problems were already reported in [July 2024](https://github.com/storj/storagenode-docker/issues/23).

**This fork's Docker image does not use that entrypoint or run storagenode-updater.** It starts the release binary bundled in the image directly and does not restore or download binaries from `/app/config/bin`. Updating the image is an explicit operator action.

The notifications database migration to version 63 was already present in official v1.165.1 and in this fork's previous v1.165.6 release; it is not new in v1.166.4. If switching back to an official image, ensure it starts a compatible binary rather than a stale persisted copy. Do not delete or alter database version records to make an older binary start. Downgrading to earlier Storj versions is not guaranteed.

### Configuration

All optional custom behavior is disabled by default. Existing settings from custom v1.160.28, v1.164.28, and v1.165.6 remain valid.

Enable manual control of log rewriting:

```yaml
hashstore.compaction.manual-log-compaction: true
```

```text
STORJ_HASHSTORE_COMPACTION_MANUAL_LOG_COMPACTION=true
```

Enable compaction salvage:

```yaml
hashstore.compaction.salvage: true
```

```text
STORJ_HASHSTORE_COMPACTION_SALVAGE=true
```

Optional target free-space reporting example:

```yaml
storage2.target-free-space: 20GB
```

```text
STORJ_STORAGE2_TARGET_FREE_SPACE=20GB
```

### Manual compaction API

```text
POST /api/sno/compaction/start
Authorization: Bearer <multinode-api-key>
```

Returns `202 Accepted` after registering the job, `401 Unauthorized` for an invalid key, `409 Conflict` if another manual job is active, and `412 Precondition Failed` if manual mode is disabled. Work continues independently of the HTTP connection. `GET /api/sno/compaction` reports the current state and latest job results.

[Storj Compaction Orchestrator](https://github.com/Aleksman4o/storj-compaction-orchestrator) groups nodes by disk, schedules sequential compactions, and displays progress and history using this API. The API format remains compatible with the previous custom releases.

### Binaries and Docker

Storagenode and Multinode are built by GitHub Actions using the unmodified official v1.166.4 `release.Dockerfile`, `release.docker-bake.hcl`, validation, and ZIP-packaging scripts. Included platforms: Linux AMD64, ARM64 and ARM; Windows AMD64; FreeBSD AMD64. The official build uses Go 1.27.3. Binaries are optimized release builds with embedded version `v1.166.4` and debug information retained.

Windows executables are not Authenticode-signed; the release archives have GitHub/Sigstore build attestations as described below. Storj Labs' Azure signing credentials are not used by this fork.

Docker images contain the same release binaries as the ZIP archives and support Linux AMD64, ARM64 and ARMv7:

```text
ghcr.io/aleksman4o/storagenode:v1.166.4
ghcr.io/aleksman4o/multinode:v1.166.4
```

The Storagenode image preserves the official container's `/app/config` and `/app/identity` layout, ports, `ADDRESS`, `EMAIL`, `WALLET`, `STORAGE`, `SETUP`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `RUN_PARAMS`, arbitrary `STORJ_*` settings, and additional command-line arguments. To switch an existing container, change its image and recreate it with the same mounts and settings. The bundled binary is not replaced by an updater and the official `config/bin` is left untouched.

To update a Compose service:

```bash
docker compose pull storagenode
docker compose up -d storagenode
```

Use a version tag to control upgrades, or `latest` to follow custom releases.

### Integrity and provenance

`sha256sums` covers the release archives and container digest files. GitHub Actions signs build provenance through Sigstore. Container images include build provenance and an SBOM; `storagenode-image-digest.txt` and `multinode-image-digest.txt` identify the exact published image manifests.

```bash
gh attestation verify storagenode_linux_amd64.zip --repo Aleksman4o/storj
sha256sum -c sha256sums --ignore-missing
```

The node console does not provide TLS itself. Keep the API on a trusted network, VPN, or HTTPS reverse proxy when using Bearer keys.
